# Local Mediabunny parser guards and extent projection

Updated: 15-10-2026. Upstream: Mediabunny 1.51.0, commit `634186fd5e2dac946bf994a955680b85aceb7709`, MPL-2.0. Original notices and LICENSE are retained.

MendoSave modifies the pinned jsDelivr bundle and the corresponding five full MPL source files supplied here:

- `isobmff-demuxer.ts`: accept only compact sample widths 4/8/16; bound expanded presentation timestamps and retained fragment samples to 1,000,000 objects; validate PCM chunk ranges against actual offsets and bound expanded chunks; skip composition offsets beyond the actual timestamp table. Before reading/materializing `stts`, `ctts`, `stsz`, `stz2`, `stss`, `stsc`, `stco`, `co64`, `tfra` and `saiz`, charge a cumulative 4,000,000-entry budget across boxes and tracks. Auxiliary encryption sample counts are charged even with a constant entry size, before retaining them for lazy resolution. Existing-table revisits in `stsc` and `tfra` also consume that budget. Sorted fragment-index duplicates are removed by linear stable compaction instead of repeated array shifting.
- `adts-reader.ts`: reject frames shorter than the ADTS header (7 bytes without CRC, 9 with CRC), preventing a reader from repeatedly seeking to the same header.
- `isobmff-misc.ts`: bound PSSH key IDs by the physical payload and the 4,000,000-entry ceiling before iteration; validate the data length. The shared helper protects both MP4 and HLS callers. MP4 additionally charges key IDs and PSSH boxes to its cumulative budget. Inline `senc` rows/revisits and both inline/lazy encryption subsamples also consume that same demuxer budget before allocation.
- `flac-demuxer.ts`: finish timestamp lookup with `null` when EOF contains no sample, releasing the reading mutex. Nonempty streams retain lazy reads and the last-packet clamp beyond their end.
- `codec-data.ts`: read AV1 OBU unsigned LEB128 lengths arithmetically, preserving the eight-byte limit and values below `2 ** 32 - 1`. Require an actual extension/length byte and a payload fitting the remaining packet before yielding. Invalid lengths throw `Invalid AV1 OBU size` through codec probing and key-packet inspection. Valid zero-size, padded-length, extension-header and size-less final OBUs remain supported.

Regular MP4 lookup additionally validates derived chunk/sample indices and bounds variable-size chunks by the physical normalized sample table. A lazy per-table `Float64Array` prefix index replaces repeated whole-chunk scans; it is created after PCM normalization and reused by all packet lookup modes. Index construction is linear in retained sample sizes; each subsequent chunk sum/offset lookup is constant time. Unsafe cumulative byte sums fail explicitly. Constant-size tables retain their arithmetic lookup and compact logical PCM representation. This index does not add an `mdat` ownership check.

The budgets apply to materialized metadata tables/revisits and each retained fragment across tracks/runs. They are not caps on a whole recording's compact PCM sample count: a constant-size `stsz` charges one entry. Valid PCM rechunking and defaults-only fragments remain supported. Files exceeding the metadata budget fail explicitly.

The two MP4 packet construction paths also expose the demuxer's existing physical sample extent as an own `packet.mendoMp4Extent` property. Its value is `Object.freeze({ offset, byteLength })`; `Object.defineProperty` leaves the property non-enumerable, non-writable and non-configurable. Regular samples use `sampleInfo.sampleOffset`/`sampleSize`; fragmented samples use `fragmentSample.byteOffset`/`byteSize`. Both metadata-only and actual-data packets pass through these construction points. This projection adds no parser, index or dependency and does not certify that a sample belongs to `mdat`: malformed container offsets are deliberately projected unchanged so callers can reject them against physical payload boundaries before trusting or saving media. Other containers and newly constructed packets receive no such property.

`PROVENANCE.json` records original and modified hashes. The complete upstream source tree is available in the versioned [npm source archive](https://registry.npmjs.org/mediabunny/-/mediabunny-1.51.0.tgz) and [Git commit](https://github.com/Vanilagy/mediabunny/tree/634186fd5e2dac946bf994a955680b85aceb7709). To work with the modified TypeScript source tree, replace `src/isobmff/isobmff-demuxer.ts`, `src/isobmff/isobmff-misc.ts`, `src/adts/adts-reader.ts`, `src/flac/flac-demuxer.ts` and `src/codec-data.ts` with the full files supplied here. Their original relative imports are retained.

The shipped bundle is obtained by deterministic local text transformation of the pinned original, without compiling TypeScript or changing the FFmpeg core. From the MendoSave repository, run:

```text
node scripts/patch-mediabunny.cjs <original-jsdelivr-bundle> <original-isobmff-demuxer.ts> <original-adts-reader.ts> <original-isobmff-misc.ts> <original-flac-demuxer.ts> <original-codec-data.ts>
```

The script checks all six original SHA-256 hashes and unique anchors before writing output. Regression tests reverse the transformations, verify the original hashes, and reapply them to reproduce the distributed files exactly. They also exercise the actual public `Input` parser using controlled valid/malformed media metadata; the allocation budget is scaled down only in the resource-guard test copy. Extent tests use the shipped bundle unchanged and cover regular/fragmented MP4, metadata/actual packets, immutable property descriptors and raw projection of corrupted sample offsets. Work-bound tests use the shipped bundle through public packet/duration/codec APIs; potentially nonterminating cases run in owned child processes with a timeout. Valid FLAC/AV1 controls are synthetic fixtures described in `tests/fixtures/README.md`. This verifies the transformation, parser guards and projection. A bit-for-bit TypeScript compilation of the generated jsDelivr bundle was not performed.
